Court No. - 91
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 2988 of 2023

Appellant :- Dharmesh Singh @ Jhallu Singh
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Appellant :- Jitendra Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sharad Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Om Prakash Tripathi,J.
Order on Short Term Bail/Parole Application No. 04 of 2023.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
This application has been moved on behalf of the appellant Dharmesh Singh @ Jhallu Singh, to release the appellant on short term bail/parole on the ground of seriousness of his son and wife.

The appellant was convicted for the offence under section 354D IPC and sentenced for two years R.I.
and also convicted under section 7/8 POCSO Act and sentenced for four years R.I. on 17.03.2023.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that record of the trial court has been summoned and complainant has been served but case has not been listed.

It is also submitted that the appellant has only son aged about 14 years suffering from high blood sugar from last two years and he has been injected by insulin into four times and his pancreas has also damaged due to lack of Dharmesh Singh @ Jhallu Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138124000/
1 better treatment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wife of the appellant is also serious patient of high blood sugar.
It is further submitted that the appellant be released for arranging money for better treatment of his son and wife.
In the report of ultrasound of son of the appellant, it has been concluded that there is resolving acute pancreatitis with minimal ascites with fatty liver.
From the papers on record, it appears that treatment of wife is going on since 12.7.2022 and treatment of son is going on from 11.8.2022.

Learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance on the judgment of Apex Court dated 08.11.2021 passed on Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary No(s). 18011 of 20211 (Tinka @ Murat Singh vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh.

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary No(s). 18011 of 20211 (Tinka @ Murat Singh vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the appellant was convicted for life imprisonment under sections 302, 201 and 376 IPC and petitioner has undergone sentence more than 10 years.
The petitioner has been granted short term bail for a period of six months for generating funds to take care of his wife.
The facts of the present case are not similar to the facts of the aforesaid case.
The appellant is in jail since 17.03.2023 and undergone about two months, one week.
Now a days, diabetes is very common disease.
The son and wife of the appellant are under treatment.
In view of the above, the grounds for short term bail/parole for the appellant is insufficient.
The short term bail/parole application is accordingly, rejected.
